chunks.title: About Dirac Flow
chunks.text: Dirac Flow is an intuitive tool for real-time tuning of specific Dirac features. It controls the runtime on the target system with minimal delay, so you can hear the effect of each change immediately. This enables an efficient workflow where you can quickly adjust and refine the sound. Which features are available depends on what has been licensed and enabled for your project in your workspace. Some features are configured by Dirac only, while others are exposed for you to adjust. This document explains how to use Dirac Flow as delivered in your setup.

chunks.title: System requirements
chunks.text: Dirac Flow requires a Windows OS computer with Microsoft Windows 11 or later as operating system. If you have an older version of Windows OS, speak to Dirac to check compatibility.

chunks.title: License
chunks.text: To access Flow and its features, you must have a software license issued for each seat (named individual). Each license is valid for a specified individual over a specified time period.

chunks.title: Names of modules and processors
chunks.text: The names of the workspaces, modules, processors and parameters in your workspace may not have the exact same name as the modules and processors described and displayed in this manual. In many cases, this documentation gives instructions for a type of processor. These instructions apply to a processor of that type that has been given a name that is applied to your specific workspace and area of use. The names and application areas of modules and processors are made according to the specification of your individual project.

chunks.title: Interface
chunks.text: The Flow interface has 4 panels: 1. Workspace panel 2. Processor panel 3. Settings panel 4. Properties panel The workspace, settings and properties panels can be hidden from view with the toggle icons in the upper right corner. A panel that is shown is displayed as blue on the icon, and a panel that is hidden is displayed as grey on the icon. Press the left side of the icon to hide/unhide the workspace panel. Press the middle part of the icon to hide/unhide the Settings panel. Press the right side of the icon to hide/unhide the properties panel. You can resize your panels by dragging the panel border toward

chunks.title: Interface
chunks.text: Settings panel. Press the right side of the icon to hide/unhide the properties panel. You can resize your panels by dragging the panel border toward the processor panel. The workspace panel can be compressed to a single column panel by pressing the Compress icon and it can be expanded back to a two-column view by pressing the Expand icon . >

chunks.title: Workspace panel
chunks.text: The workspace panel (1) has all the configurations, settings, processors, stages, A/B comparison tool, and parameter diagrams. It is in the workspace panel that you select the configuration you want to use, select which processor you want to inspect/edit, and select which parameter diagrams you want to inspect to verify the setup.

chunks.title: Processor panel
chunks.text: The processor panel (2) is where the processors, settings, diagrams etc. are shown. It is the principal working area that is always displayed.

chunks.title: Settings panel
chunks.text: In the settings panel (3) a number of settings, interface parameters, and connections are handled. This is also the area where the performance can be measured, and logging of events in the connections can be done in case of connection issues. This is also the location of the Media Player, the built-in audio file player that can be used for playback when tuning. Each tab holds a separate setup of parameters. Refer to the chapters in this manual for more information.

chunks.title: Properties panel
chunks.text: The properties panel (4) shows the properties of the processor, and if applicable, it shows presets, the filters of the processor including the filter that is sent to the device, filter information, and any changes that have been made to a filter.

chunks.title: Your Workspace
chunks.text: To open a workspace, go to the top menu File/Open and select the .fws file you want to work with. The workspace contains the specified number of configurations and show the specified processors of the signal chain for a selected configuration.

chunks.title: To set parameter values
chunks.text: When a value must be set or adjusted, use one of the follwing methods to set the value. The method options can vary, and depends on the type of value that is set. A. List value: Click on the field, choose a new value from the list and click the selected value to confirm. B. List value: Put the mouse pointer over the field and use the mouse scroll wheel to go though the list of values one step at a time. C. Numeric value: Click in the field and use the mouse scroll wheel up to increase the value or the scroll wheel down to decrease the value by

chunks.title: To set parameter values
chunks.text: Click in the field and use the mouse scroll wheel up to increase the value or the scroll wheel down to decrease the value by specific increments. D. Numericvalue: Click in the field and use keyboard arrow up key to increase the value or the arrow down key to decrease the value by specific increments. E. Numericvalue: Click in the field and use the keyboard PgUp key up to increase the value or the PgDn key to decrease the value by specific increments. F. Numericvalue: If you know the exact value you want, click on the field value and type the new value. Press Enter to confirm. G. Numericvalue: Click

chunks.title: To set parameter values
chunks.text: If you know the exact value you want, click on the field value and type the new value. Press Enter to confirm. G. Numericvalue: Click on the field arrow up to increase the value or field arrow down to decrease the value by specific increments with each click.

chunks.title: Interface Parameters
chunks.text: Each of the biquad filter parameters in all processors can be made available as an interface parameter that can be changed by external input, for example a user interface. If the settings are set as Interface parameters, they have a lock icon on them in the processor panel and their values are editable only on the Interface parameters tab in the settings panel (3).

chunks.title: Processor settings
chunks.text: In the top menu Tools/Options you can make global settings for all the processors in Flow. Peak level hold time sets the amount of time the peak is held after the level starts dropping. Samples to trigger clipping sets the level for how many samples are permitted to go over the threshold before the clipping indicator shows that the threshold has been breached. RMS +3dB (Root Mean Square) adds 3 dB to the signal energy to make it display approximately the same value as an amplitude display. Infinite hold lets you keep the peak value infinitely and not let it fall. If you double-click on a level meter, it resets

chunks.title: Processor settings
chunks.text: amplitude display. Infinite hold lets you keep the peak value infinitely and not let it fall. If you double-click on a level meter, it resets the clipping indicator and releases the hold.

chunks.title: Filter errors
chunks.text: If a filter has one or more errors, the processor selection in the workspace panel shows an exclamation mark. Put the mouse pointer over the exclamation mark to show the error information. If there are several errors, the error information is for the first error. When the first error is resolved, the next error information is shown. When all errors are resolved, the exclamation mark is no longer shown, and the filter can be used for the processor. Possible filter errors can be, for example, incorrect dimensions of the filter, unsupported sample rates, incorrect filter properties, incorrect number of layers, incorrect resampling type, incorrect number of FIR taps, or too

chunks.title: Filter errors
chunks.text: incorrect dimensions of the filter, unsupported sample rates, incorrect filter properties, incorrect number of layers, incorrect resampling type, incorrect number of FIR taps, or too many biquads.

chunks.title: Bypass
chunks.text: If a processor is to be bypassed in the signal chain, you must press the Bypass icon next to the name of the processor in the processor panel: When the bypass is set, the bypass icon becomes orange, and the icon is also shown in front of the processor name in the signal chain:

chunks.title: Shared processors
chunks.text: If a processor in a workspace is shared between configurations, it displays a small icon in front of the processor name. The icon indicates the type of sharing and the channel requirements between configurations: Shared, requires the same number of channels in all configurations. Shared, supports different number of channels in different configurations.

chunks.title: Theme
chunks.text: The theme of Flow can be changed from the default Light mode to Dark mode. Go to top menu Tools/Theme to select the new theme. This user manual has screenshots and descriptions for Light mode. If you use Flow in Dark mode, note that the colour scheme is different or inverted to what it is in Light mode. For example, if an unselected filter cell is described as “dark grey” in Light mode, the colour of the filter cell can be “light grey” in Dark mode. Flow in Light mode Flow in Dark mode

chunks.title: Software update for Flow
chunks.text: When there is a software update available for Flow, a flag appears in the top right corner of the interface. Hover over the flag with the mouse pointer to view the update message. Press the flag to start the update of the software. NOTE: there is no roll-back to a previous version of Flow after an update. It’s recomended to use the latest version of Flow. It’s compatable with DPL 5.0.0 and later plus some special versions of DPL 4. Old versions of Flow may not be compatible with newer DPLs.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Power EQ processor is a biquad equaliser that can be used for various purposes (User EQ, Loudness and others). The Power EQ makes it possible to set filter values for each biquad filter in the applied use of the processor in the audio system.

chunks.title: To set biquad filter values
chunks.text: Make sure that the checkbox (1) of the biquad filter is checked to enable the filter. If the checkbox is not checked, the biquad filter will not affect the output. Click on the enabled biquad filter you want to adjust. The active biquad filter has a blue border around it and the plot point (7) in the plot area is highlighted. You can also use the mouse pointer to hover over the biquad plot point in the plot area to make the biquad filter active. When a value for a biquad filter parameter is changed, the plot area adjusts and shows the new value in the plot. Right-clicking a biquad

chunks.title: To set biquad filter values
chunks.text: When a value for a biquad filter parameter is changed, the plot area adjusts and shows the new value in the plot. Right-clicking a biquad filter will provide the option to copy and paste all biquad filter values. You can set a new value with one of the methods described in the Introduction chapter, or use the biquad filter plot point as described below.

chunks.title: Filter type
chunks.text: The Filter type (2) field lets you choose a new filter type for the biquad filter from the list.

chunks.title: Center frequency
chunks.text: The Center frequency (3) field sets a new center frequency value between 10 and 20000 Hz. You can also click on the highlighted biquad filter plot point (7) in the plot area and drag the point laterally to the new value point.

chunks.title: Gain
chunks.text: The Gain (4) field lets you set a new gain value for the biquad filter. This value can be set with positive or negative values, normally ranging from -25 to 15 dB. A. To set the value with the precision of 1 decimal point (0,1), click on the highlighted biquad filter plot point (7) in the plot area. Drag the point vertically to the new Gain point. B. To set the Gain value manually, click the arrow up to increase the value, or the arrow down to decrease the value.

chunks.title: Q-factor
chunks.text: In the Q-factor (5) field you can set a new Q-factor value between 0,1 and 30. You can also use the mouse pointer to hover over the biquad filter plot point (7) in the plot area. Use the mouse scroll wheel to increase or decrease the value.

chunks.title: Slope
chunks.text: If a Filter type (2) has a Slope (6) value, the field becomes editable. In the Slope (6) field you can set a new slope value for the biquad filter from the list. NOTE: a greater slope value increases the number of biquads used.

chunks.title: Tools
chunks.text: The output Gain (8) sets the value for the module. The Export (9) tool is used when you want to export the frequency and gain values to a .txt file. This function may not be available in all workspaces. The Equalizer curve tool (10) lets you use the plot area to make settings. The Zoom and pan tool (11) helps you zoom in on a selection in the plot area.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Filter inspection processor type is where filters with set values for a number of filter cells can be imported and inspected. These processors are part of Dirac’s filter technologies, for example Bass control, Harmony, Unison and others.

chunks.title: To import a filter
chunks.text: Press the Import filter button (7), and select a file in the correct file format for the processor (.json, XML Text, or XML Binary). You can import multiple filters into the view to inspect them one at a time. Press the file name (8) to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-6) and properties panel (10). The filter that is shown in the panels has a blue border. To send a specific filter to the device, press the dot (9) before the filter file name. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent to the device.

chunks.title: Filter errors
chunks.text: If a filter that is sent to the device has one or more errors, the processor selection in the workspace panel shows an exclamation mark. Put the mouse pointer over the exclamation mark to show the error information. If there are several errors, only the first is shown; when it’s resolved, the next appears. Once all errors are resolved, the exclamation mark disappears and the filter can be used for the processor. Possible filter errors can be, for example, incorrect dimensions of the filter, unsupported sample rates, incorrect filter properties, incorrect number of layers, incorrect resampling type, incorrect number of FIR taps, or too many biquads.

chunks.title: Frequency/Time
chunks.text: Press Frequency or Time (1) to select view type. In the plot area, Frequency shows the magnitude response and Time shows the impulse response for the selected filter cell and layer.

chunks.title: Layer
chunks.text: If the filter has more than one layer, you can select a layer (2) to view it in the panel. All layers are processed in parallel, where each individual layer is processed at an individual sample rate. To view the sum of all layers, press Full rate in the layer selection (2).

chunks.title: Sample rate
chunks.text: Select the Sample rate (3) you want to view. You can choose between 48000 Hz and 44100 Hz.

chunks.title: Filter cells
chunks.text: Click on an unselected, dark grey filter cell (4) in the processor panel to select it. A selected filter cell (5) has a blue border, and the curve is shown in the plot area (6) in the the same colour as the cell colour. To show several filter cells simultaneously, press CTRL and click on the unselected filter cell you want to select and show in the plot area. NOTE: An unused, light grey filter cell is not clickable.

chunks.title: To export a filter
chunks.text: Right-click the filter you want to export (8 or 9). Select the applicable file format for this filter, and save it to your chosen location. NOTE: Filter export requires an applicable licence.

chunks.title: To remove a filter
chunks.text: Press the minus symbol (11) on the filter you want to remove from the panels. In the popup window, press Delete if you want to remove it, or press Keep to cancel.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Channel EQ is a biquad equaliser that allows you to assign different EQ settings to different sets of channels by grouping them. Each group shares a unique, editable EQ configuration. Groups are created and managed using the channel-group matrix.

chunks.title: To create/import a filter
chunks.text: Press the Create filter button (5). You can choose to: A. Import. Select the .XML processor file you want to view and edit. You can import multiple filters into the view to inspect them one at a time. B. Create new. Create a blank, editable filter and edit it as described below. To import filters with Dirac IO, refer to the Dirac IO page and the Dirac IO section in the FilterLab User manual. In the Properties panel, under the Imported with Dirac IO section or the Editable section, press the file name (6) to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-4) and properties panel (8). The filter

chunks.title: To create/import a filter
chunks.text: or the Editable section, press the file name (6) to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-4) and properties panel (8). The filter that is shown in the panels has a blue border. To send a specific filter to the device, press the dot (7) before the filter file name. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent to the device. If the imported filter has fewer channels or fewer biquad filters per group than specified in the properties, it is padded with channels and default biquad filters up to the required amount. If the filter has more channels or more biquad filters than allowed by

chunks.title: To create/import a filter
chunks.text: padded with channels and default biquad filters up to the required amount. If the filter has more channels or more biquad filters than allowed by the Channel EQ properties, only entries within the allowed range are imported. If multiple channels share identical biquad-filter sets, they are automatically grouped during import. Note that importing a filter may cause the groups to be in another order than when the filter was exported.

chunks.title: Grouping channels
chunks.text: The channel-group matrix contains one draggable cell per column (1), representing a channel. A selected cell has a blue border, and the curve is shown in the plot area (10) in the the same colour as the cell colour. Moving the cell to a row assigns the channel to that row’s group. All the channels on the same row are in one group and share EQ settings. There can be a maximum number of groups equal to the number of channels. When dragging and dropping a channel onto an empty row the channel retains its existing EQ settings. Dragging a channel onto a row that already contains channels causes the

chunks.title: Grouping channels
chunks.text: a channel onto an empty row the channel retains its existing EQ settings. Dragging a channel onto a row that already contains channels causes the channel to inherit the EQ settings of the destination group. The channel’s previous EQ settings are then replaced. The top row is the ungrouped row (2). In the ungrouped row every channel is treated independently and has its own EQ settings. When dragging and dropping a channel onto the ungrouped row the channel retains its existing EQ settings.

chunks.title: Matrix rows
chunks.text: Pressing the “add group”-button (3) or dragging a cell to that row creates a new row. Right clicking any group label (4) will provide the option of removing the row. Any channel on the removed row will be ungrouped and retain its EQ settings. Double clicking a group label will give you the option of renaming a group.

chunks.title: To set biquad filter values
chunks.text: Details on configuring biquad filters are provided in the biquad-filter section of the Power EQ page.

chunks.title: Lock for editing
chunks.text: Filters can be locked for editing. When you are satisfied with a filter, right-click it and select Lock for editing to prevent unintentional changes. A locked filter shows a padlock icon (11); an unlocked filter has no icon. To make the filter editable again, right-click it and select Unlock. A filter that is imported from a file is locked by default, but it can be unlocked. A filter that is imported with Dirac IO is always locked and cannot be unlocked, because it is controlled by the client. If you want to edit the filter, duplicate it to create an editable copy.

chunks.title: To duplicate a filter
chunks.text: If you want to make an exact copy of a filter, right-click on the filter name (6 or 7) and select Duplicate. The copy of the filter is shown in the parameters panel, with a number after the file name.

chunks.title: To export a filter
chunks.text: Right-click the filter you want to export (6 or 7). Select the applicable file format for this filter, and save it to your chosen location. Exported filters do not contain group names and will therefore not contain a name when imported. NOTE: Filter export requires an applicable licence.

chunks.title: To remove a filter
chunks.text: Press the minus symbol (9) on the filter you want to remove from the panels. In the popup window, press Delete if you want to remove it, or press Keep to cancel.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Matrix mixer processor type is where each input channel can be mapped to output channels and adjusted for delay and gain. This processor type can be used for Matrix mixer, Fader, and Balance processors and others.

chunks.title: To create/import a filter
chunks.text: Press the Create filter button (11). You can choose to: A. Import. Select the .XML processor file you want to view and edit. You can import multiple filters into the view to inspect them one at a time. B. Create new. Create a blank, editable filter and add filter cells and values as described below. To import filters with Dirac IO, refer to the Dirac IO page and the Dirac IO section in the FilterLab User manual. In the Properties panel, under the Imported with Dirac IO section or the Editable section, press the file name (12) to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-10) and properties panel

chunks.title: To create/import a filter
chunks.text: Dirac IO section or the Editable section, press the file name (12) to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-10) and properties panel (14). The filter that is shown in the panels has a blue border. To send a specific filter to the device, press the dot (13) before the filter file name. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent to the device.

chunks.title: To edit a filter
chunks.text: If you have imported a filter, or created a new filter, you can add and remove filter cells, and adjust the values for them.

chunks.title: Lock for editing
chunks.text: Filters can be locked for editing. When you are satisfied with a filter, right-click it and select Lock for editing to prevent unintentional changes. A locked filter shows a padlock icon (16); an unlocked filter has no icon. To make the filter editable again, right-click it and select Unlock. A filter that is imported from a file is locked by default, but it can be unlocked. A filter that is imported with Dirac IO is always locked and cannot be unlocked, because it is controlled by the client. If you want to edit the filter, duplicate it to create an editable copy.

chunks.title: Mute/Solo
chunks.text: Press M on the input/output channel(s) you want to mute. You can mute multiple channels. Press S on the input/output channel(s) you want to listen to on their own. This mutes all other channels. You can select multiple channels as Solo channels.

chunks.title: 1/N
chunks.text: If there are two or more filter cells for an output, you can check the checkbox 1/N (4) to merge the filter cell values for the output channel to prevent clipping.

chunks.title: Filter cell
chunks.text: Click on an unselected, dark grey filter cell (5) in the processor panel to select it. A selected filter cell has a blue border, and the cell information is shown below the matrix if it is editable. To move a filter cell, drag it to an unused filter cell and drop it in the cell. To add a new filter cell, right-click on an unused, light grey filter cell and select Add element. To copy an existing filter cell, right-click it and select Copy, then right-click an unused filter cell and select Paste. You can also press CTRL, click the filter cell you want to copy, and drag it to

chunks.title: Filter cell
chunks.text: right-click an unused filter cell and select Paste. You can also press CTRL, click the filter cell you want to copy, and drag it to an unused filter cell.

chunks.title: Show attenuated gain
chunks.text: Check the checkbox Show attenuated gain (6) to display the real gain for all filter cells.

chunks.title: Cell information
chunks.text: The information in the filter cells in the matrix can be adjusted under Cell information (7). To adapt to a screen resolution, it can show Full information, Compact information (values only), or None.

chunks.title: Invert phase
chunks.text: Check the Invert phase (8) checkbox to switch the polarity of the channel by 180°.

chunks.title: Gain
chunks.text: Move the Gain (9) fader up to increase the gain value, and down to decrease the gain value of the filter cell.

chunks.title: Delay
chunks.text: The Delay (10) to the output channel can be adjusted with high precision to a value in milliseconds. Delay ms x1 sets the integer digits, 0-max. delay. Delay ms x0.1 sets the first fractional digit, 0-9. Delay ms x0.01 sets the second fractional digit, 0-9. Total shows the combined sum of all three delay settings, for example 8.95 ms. You can also use the arrows up to increase and arrow down to decrease the delay by a full integer digit.

chunks.title: Lock for editing
chunks.text: Filters can be locked for editing. When you are satisfied with a filter, right-click it and select Lock for editing to prevent unintentional changes. A locked filter shows a padlock icon; (16) an unlocked filter has no icon. To make the filter editable again, right-click it and select Unlock. A filter that is imported from a file is locked by default, but it can be unlocked. A filter that is imported with Dirac IO is always locked and cannot be unlocked, because it is controlled by the client. If you want to edit the filter, duplicate it to create an editable copy.

chunks.title: To duplicate a filter
chunks.text: If you want to make an exact copy of a filter, right-click on the filter name (12 or 13) and select Duplicate. The copy of the filter is shown in the parameters panel, with a number after the file name.

chunks.title: To export a filter
chunks.text: Right-click the filter you want to export (12 or 13). Select the applicable file format for this filter, and save it to your chosen location. NOTE: Filter export requires an applicable licence.

chunks.title: To remove a filter
chunks.text: Press the minus symbol (15) on the filter you want to remove from the panels. In the popup window, press Delete if you want to remove it, or press Keep to cancel.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Dirac IO makes it possible to create filters in FilterLab and import them in Flow to display them in real time in specified processors.

chunks.title: To import a filter with Dirac IO
chunks.text: When filters have been created in FilterLab, they can be exported from FilterLab, imported into Flow with the Dirac IO connection. The following instructions are for an existing server connection between FilterLab and Flow. For instructions on server implementation, refer to the section on Dirac IO integration in the FilterLab User manual.

chunks.title: Set the server in Flow
chunks.text: 1. Go to the Settings panel and press the Dirac IO Servers (11) tab. 2. Set the server you want to use to ON (12).

chunks.title: Set the server in FilterLab
chunks.text: This must be set the first time the Dirac IO connection is made. Depending on setup, the setting can be saved. 1. Press the Dirac IO info (1) tab. 2. Press the update UPnP icon (2). 3. In the UPnP field (3), select from the list the name of the server you set to ON in Flow. 4. Press the button Get server info (4). 5. Make sure that there are no errors or warnings in the server connection. An error is shown with a red icon you can click on to get more information.

chunks.title: To do a Dirac IO export in FilterLab
chunks.text: 1. In the top menu, go to Filter export/Dirac IO export. 2. In the popup, select/deselect the sections you want to export/exclude (5), and check the checkbox (6) below the section if you want an automated or continuous feed of data from the sections in FilterLab. NOTE: In the export popup, a section is yellow if it is exported for the first time, if there are changes made to the section since last export, or if a different slot than the previous export is selected. A section is green if your previous export was sent to the same slot and there are no changes made to the section. 3. In

chunks.title: To do a Dirac IO export in FilterLab
chunks.text: A section is green if your previous export was sent to the same slot and there are no changes made to the section. 3. In the Slot selection area (7), select the server slot that you want to send the export to. You can choose to give the selected slot a new name (8). NOTE: A slot contains the data for each of the selected sections of the export. Example: To do A/B testing you can export version A for each of the sections to slot 1, and version B of each of the sections to slot 2. You can then quickly switch between slot 1 and slot 2 in

chunks.title: To do a Dirac IO export in FilterLab
chunks.text: slot 1, and version B of each of the sections to slot 2. You can then quickly switch between slot 1 and slot 2 in Flow to test the different versions. 4. Check the checkbox Re-export all (9) if you want all the filter data exported in full to Flow. 5. Press Export (10) to send the filter through Dirac IO. NOTE: An export overwrites any previous export to the selected slot.

chunks.title: To do a Dirac IO import in Flow
chunks.text: 1. Go to the Dirac IO Servers (11) tab in the Settings panel. 2. Press the dot (13) by the slot name you sent your export to. An enabled slot has a blue dot. 3. Press the cogwheel of the server (14) to view the server properties, imported sections and their parameters. You can also adjust the number of slots or stop the server. 4. Go to the properties panel and press the Dirac IO filter name (15) to show it in the processor and parameter panels. The filter must have a blue border. 5. Press the dot (16) in front of the Dirac IO filter to send the filter

chunks.title: To do a Dirac IO import in Flow
chunks.text: parameter panels. The filter must have a blue border. 5. Press the dot (16) in front of the Dirac IO filter to send the filter to the device. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent.

chunks.title: To show filter adjustments in real time
chunks.text: To show changes made in FilterLab in real time in Flow, make sure these parameters are set: In FilterLab: 1. Set Auto export/Continuous (6) for each section in the export to a selected slot in Flow. In Flow: 2. Enable the correct slot (13) on the server on the Dirac IO Servers tab. 3. Click the Dirac IO filter name (15) in the parameters panel to show the filter in the processor panel. The Dirac IO filter must have a blue border. 4. Press the dot (16) in front of the Dirac IO filter name. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent to the device.

chunks.title: To edit a filter
chunks.text: A filter imported with Dirac IO to Flow is in most cases editable only in FilterLab.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Interface parameters are selected parameters that can be changed by external input, for example a user interface. The change triggers a re-calculation of the parameter. The new calculation value is sent to the signal chain that executes the change in the output. The parameters on the Interface parameters tab (1) in the settings panel are the parameters that can be set up to be changed from the device user interface.

chunks.title: Parameters
chunks.text: When a signal chain processor has a parameter that can be changed externally, the processor shows the parameter field as locked for editing with a lock icon next to the field in the processor panel. The parameters can be configured as required.

chunks.title: To view interface parameters
chunks.text: 1. Press the Interface parameters tab (1) in the settings panel to view the Interface parameters in the workspace. 2. If you want to see the automatically generated parameters, check the checkbox Show auto generated (2). 3. Select parameter view (3). You can choose to show All configurations (all parameters in all configurations), Active configuration (relevant parameters for the selected configuration), or a specific configuration. 4. If you want to optimise the view, you can click on the arrow icon (4) to minimise a parameter in the view, or click on the parameter name to expand it to normal view.

chunks.title: To view interface parameter diagrams
chunks.text: Interface parameters are defined in the interface parameter diagrams. NOTE: An interface parameter diagram can contain more than one interface parameter. 1. To view the parameter diagram of an interface parameter and its processors: A. Click on the shortcut (5) on the interface parameter to go directly to the diagram. B. Click on the parameter diagram (6) you want to show. If necessary, select the Parameter diagram view (7). 2. To show the values that are sent from the parameter through the processors to the signal chain processors, check the checkbox Show wire values (10). 3. Double-click on a processor (9) or click on a processor name in the parameter

chunks.title: To view interface parameter diagrams
chunks.text: signal chain processors, check the checkbox Show wire values (10). 3. Double-click on a processor (9) or click on a processor name in the parameter processor list (8) to go to the processor settings view (11). If a processor in the Parameter diagram cannot be double-clicked, it does not have a view.

chunks.title: Interface parameters panel
chunks.text: An interface parameter is shown as a slider or a switch. The slider can be moved up to increase the value or down to decrease the value of the parameter. The switch is an On/Off button that has two positions. The change to a parameter in the panel is the same as the change an end user makes on the user interface.

chunks.title: Processors
chunks.text: The settings of an interface parameter diagram processor are in some cases editable. Go to a processor settings view (11) as described above. If the processor settings are editable, you can adjust the values in the view. Some of the settings are view-only that for example show the processor name, parameter ID, type, or the mapping to the signal chain processor. There are different types of processors that have different settings available, for example Slew rate limiter, On/off, and Lookup table. If there is an icon before a lookup table processor in the parameter processor list (8), the lookup table processor can be: Restricted for editing during tuning Not editable

chunks.title: Processors
chunks.text: icon before a lookup table processor in the parameter processor list (8), the lookup table processor can be: Restricted for editing during tuning Not editable during tuning Shared, can be used in multiple interface parameter diagrams

chunks.title: Slew rate limiter
chunks.text: When a user uses an interface parameter to increase or decrease the output, the Slew rate limiter can be set to limit the rate or time between the old value and the new value: A. Fixed rate. It sets a maximum rate change per second. B. Fixed time. It sets the time to reach the new value.

chunks.title: On/off
chunks.text: The On/off parameter has two settings: On or Off, where one of the values can be set as default. One application area of this processor type is Mute.

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: A lookup table processor for an interface parameter can give more control over how the parameter value change is calculated before it is sent to the signal chain processor for output. You can see the Input type (12) and Output type (13) of the lookup table in the processor panel. The lookup table processor settings view also shows the ranges of the input and output (14). A lookup table has a set number of points (15). The table can use some of the points, or all of them. The amount of points can be seen under Num points (21) in the properties panel. 1. Click the Add point (16) button

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: all of them. The amount of points can be seen under Num points (21) in the properties panel. 1. Click the Add point (16) button to add another point within the set number of points. If the button is grey and not clickable, the maximum number of points has been set for the table. 2. Click the Remove point (17) icon on a point to remove it. 3. Click the Rescale (18) button to set new minimum and maximum values for the lookup table. In the popup window, set the new values and click Rescale to recalculate the table, or Cancel to discard the changes. NOTE: Rescale lets you set

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: the popup window, set the new values and click Rescale to recalculate the table, or Cancel to discard the changes. NOTE: Rescale lets you set the table values outside the connected input and output range. To change the values in a lookup table To change some of the values of a lookup table, you can click in the field you want to change and type a new value. You can also use the arrow up to increase or arrow down to decrease the value by a set increment. Alternatively, you can click on the value and use the mouse scroll wheel (if enabled) and scroll up to increase or down

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: a set increment. Alternatively, you can click on the value and use the mouse scroll wheel (if enabled) and scroll up to increase or down to decrease the value. To export and import a lookup table file If a lookup table has the correct values and number of points you want to use in another lookup table processor, you can export the lookup table so that it can be imported to another table. 1. Click the Export table (19) icon. 2. Select Export to file to export the table as a .paramMap file. A file window opens. 3. Set the file name and location where the file is to be

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: to export the table as a .paramMap file. A file window opens. 3. Set the file name and location where the file is to be saved. 4. Go to the lookup table processor you want to import it to. 5. Click the Import table (20) icon and select Import from file to import a lookup table file to a lookup table processor. 6. Select the correct .paramMap file or a correctly structured .csv file in the file window. 7. Press Open to import the file to the lookup table processor. NOTE: If the import is made correctly, the imported values overwrite any existing values and are shown in the lookup

chunks.title: Lookup table
chunks.text: to the lookup table processor. NOTE: If the import is made correctly, the imported values overwrite any existing values and are shown in the lookup table processor. If there are errors in the import, an error prompt is shown with more information. Correct the error, and do a new import. If the number of points of the import is different from what the original export was, the new number of points is displayed if it is within the set amount of points.
