chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Workspace Settings tab (1) has the device connection settings that are used for setting up the the connection from Flow to a device for tuning.

chunks.title: To connect
chunks.text: To connect Flow to the device: 1. Press the Workspace Settings (1) tab in the settings panel. 2. If you process audio on your computer or stream audio from the Flow Media player, click on the Audio Settings (2) button to open the Audio settings application. When connected, the loudspeaker icon is shown as at the top of the screen. 3. Press the Update available connections (4). 4. In the Connection field (5), select from the list the type of connection you require: A. Local. The setup connects locally on your computer only, and the IP address and port are set automatically. B. Manual. You must type in the IP

chunks.title: To connect
chunks.text: The setup connects locally on your computer only, and the IP address and port are set automatically. B. Manual. You must type in the IP address and Port (6) of the device manually. C. Specific network-connected device that is shown in the list. The IP address and port are set automatically. 5. Press the Connect (7) button to connect to the device. The connection status display (8) is shown next to the Connect (7) button on the Workspace Settings tab, and at the top of the screen (3). When Flow is not connected to a device, the connection status display is shown as disconnected. When the connection is in progress,

chunks.title: To connect
chunks.text: the screen (3). When Flow is not connected to a device, the connection status display is shown as disconnected. When the connection is in progress, the connection status changes shape and the display is yellow: If the connection is made correctly, the connection status display (3, 8) changes shape again and is marked in green. If the connection failed, the connection status display (3, 8) is shown as red. To get more information on any errors, start logging the device connection. For instructions, refer to the section below on logging. If the connection was made correctly, but the target configuration is incompatible with the processor library, you may have a

chunks.title: To connect
chunks.text: the section below on logging. If the connection was made correctly, but the target configuration is incompatible with the processor library, you may have a version of the processor library and a version of the RT Core of the device that cannot function correctly together for all processors. The connection status display is shown as green, but the Compatibility connection data and the incompatible processors are marked in red. A popup window is shown with more information. Make sure that the target configuration file, the processor library and the device runtime are compatible.

chunks.title: Include all configurations
chunks.text: The checkbox Include all configurations (9) is checked by default, and lets you send all the configurations of your Workspace to the connected device. If the checkbox is not checked, only the selected configuration is sent to the device.

chunks.title: Interface parameter tuning on device
chunks.text: Check the checkbox Interface parameter tuning on device (10) to make the calculations for the interface parameter directly on the device.

chunks.title: Update DSP resources manually
chunks.text: Check the checkbox Update DSP resources manually (11) if you want to manually update the resources sent between the device, Audio Settings and Flow. This can be useful if you have a very large workspace and work on a slow connection. The automatic transfer of signal chain data is stopped, and the resources are updated only when you press the button Update resources (12). In manual update mode, the signal chain icon has an update icon that is green when the signal chain is up-to-date in the ACS (audio control service) for the connected plugins, devices and Flow. If the signal chain icon is red, the signal chain is not

chunks.title: Update DSP resources manually
chunks.text: in the ACS (audio control service) for the connected plugins, devices and Flow. If the signal chain icon is red, the signal chain is not synchronized with the ACS and you must press the Update resources (12) button.

chunks.title: Connection data
chunks.text: The connection data (13) of the Workspace Settings tab shows information about the connection and the files sent to the device. Compatibility shows if the target configuration and processor library and compatible or incompatible. For more information, refer to the section above on how to connect. DSP resource shows the speed of how fast the response is from the device for the DAR files that are sent to the device from Flow. Parameters shows if the connected device supports tuning using module parameters. If the connected device does not support module parameters, changes that are made in Flow can only be updated by sending a new DAR file to the

chunks.title: Connection data
chunks.text: connected device does not support module parameters, changes that are made in Flow can only be updated by sending a new DAR file to the device. Probes shows if the connected device supports information about instantaneous signal levels at points in the signal chain. These values are often shown in Processor views that use level meters. Tuning DAR size shows the size of the DAR file used during tuning. Full DAR size shows the size of the full DAR file. Dynamic memory size shows how much device memory is used for processing.

chunks.title: Noise
chunks.text: The Noise settings (14) of the Workspace Settings tab shows information about evaluation noise. Noise-free tuning shows if tuning without evaluation noise is enabled, disabled, or pending (waiting for data). The evaluation noise event will be checked against the evaluation license key at intervals to verify if the license is valid and the tuning can be made noise-free. Evaluation noise sets the interval of the evaluation noise that is sent to the device. The evaluation noise can be set to Periodic (regular intervals) or Randomized (irregular intervals within a longer time span).

chunks.title: Performance measurement
chunks.text: The Performance tab in the Settings panel in Flow has settings for the performance measurement of the processors. This is useful for an analysis of the connection and possible performance congestions. When performance measurement is set to On, Flow shows the Min load, Max load and Avg load for the entire connection at the top of the screen next to the connection status display (3). To view the performance of a specific processor, click on the processor in the workspace panel. A box with the performance values is shown on the Performance tab. The performance measurement can be made more precise with these settings: Ticks/second. Sets the amount of ticks

chunks.title: Performance measurement
chunks.text: performance values is shown on the Performance tab. The performance measurement can be made more precise with these settings: Ticks/second. Sets the amount of ticks per second. The value must correspond to the actual amount of ticks that are possible for the ACS. Clock frequency. Sets the clock frequency for the ACS. When the correct clock frequency is set, the performance measurement values at the top of the screen are also shown in MCPS (mega cycles per second). Update speed sets the speed of the performance measurement. If you work on a slow connection, set the update speed to slow.

chunks.title: Logging
chunks.text: Flow logs events continuously. The Logging tab in the Settings panel shows the log messages, and is useful for troubleshooting a connection to identify issues and get more information about them. Set Logging on device to On to also log events on the device itself. This gives you control over the resources used for logging, because you can filter what is logged on the device before the data is sent to Flow, rather than filtering only in the list. Filter on device lets you choose the log level and the components to log on the device. Filter in list lets you filter the levels and components that are shown in

chunks.title: Logging
chunks.text: the log level and the components to log on the device. Filter in list lets you filter the levels and components that are shown in the log message list in Flow. Use the Filter text field to show only messages that contain specified text, and use Search to find and step through matching rows with the arrow buttons Press Clear to clear the log message list. Turn on Stream logs to file to continuously write the log to a file on your computer, and press Browse to set the Stream destination. This lets you open and inspect the log in the text editor of your choice. Press Copy to copy

chunks.title: Logging
chunks.text: Browse to set the Stream destination. This lets you open and inspect the log in the text editor of your choice. Press Copy to copy the log messaes to the cliboard, or press Save to save the log to a file on your computer.

chunks.title: To disconnect
chunks.text: If you want to stop an existing connection, click the Disconnect (7) button. This stops the connection, and the connection status display is set to disconnected.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The DSP Resources export is where configurations and interface parameters can be exported to be transferred to a device for tuning or installation.

chunks.title: To export DSP resources
chunks.text: Save your current workspace. Then go to the top menu to DSP Resources/Export DSP resources. A separate window opens.

chunks.title: To do a quick export
chunks.text: In the Export DSP Resources window: 1. In the Legal information area, set the Project name (2) and Manufacturer name (3) that Flow is licensed to. Refer to the section on Legal information below for more information. 2. Check the checkbox for each configuration that you want to export as files. 3. If you want to create separate files for each configuration, check the checkbox Create separate resource for each configuration (9). 4. Select Target folder (12) on your computer where you want to save the exported files. 5. Set the Signing (13). Refer to the section on File creation below for more information. 6. Make sure the Resulting files

chunks.title: To do a quick export
chunks.text: the exported files. 5. Set the Signing (13). Refer to the section on File creation below for more information. 6. Make sure the Resulting files (14) are as you set them (one large file / one file per configuration). NOTE: The export file pairs must be kept together, as both files are required for successfully running the files on the device. 7. Press the Export button (15) to export the files.

chunks.title: To do an export with specific settings
chunks.text: If you want to do an export with more information than a quick export, you can export with specific settings and save the export settings as an export recipe.

chunks.title: Legal information
chunks.text: The text in the Legal information area is used for legal information connected to software licensing. Project name (2) refers to, for example, the name of the product model that is on the Flow software license. Manufacturer name (3) refers to the company name that Flow is licensed to. Author. The user that is logged in is set automatically as the author of the files.

chunks.title: Meta data
chunks.text: Meta data are features with values that are applied in a specified way in an integration with a device. Meta data is project-specific, and requires a customised setup. To use meta data for your project, speak to Dirac.

chunks.title: Configurations, interface parameters, and filters
chunks.text: The configuration that is selected in Flow is also selected automatically for export. If you want to include all workspace configurations in the export, check the checkbox at the top of the list of configurations to select all. If you want to select specific configurations, check the checkbox (7) for each of the configurations you want to include in the export. If you want to set all interface parameters to their default value for the export, check the checkbox Revert all interface parameters to default value (8). NOTE: this setting has a direct effect and will set all interface parameters to default in the ongoing processing. If you want to

chunks.title: Configurations, interface parameters, and filters
chunks.text: value (8). NOTE: this setting has a direct effect and will set all interface parameters to default in the ongoing processing. If you want to have each configuration as a separate file in the export, check the checkbox Create separate resource for each configuration (9). If a Filter inspection processor has more than one filter, you can select to create a separate file for each filter. Select the filter processor from the drop-down list in the Separate resource per filter (10) field. NOTE: you cannot check the checkbox Create separate resource for each configuration (9) and select Separate resource per filter (10) simultaneously.

chunks.title: File creation
chunks.text: Base file name. If you want to change the name part of the export files, you can edit the name in the Base file name (11) field. The export file names are set with the edited Base file name as the new file name. Target folder. The system sets automatically a folder where the files will be saved. To set a different folder for the exported files, press the Browse (12) button and select a new folder in the window. Press Select folder to confirm. Signing. The Signing (13) of the files is preset to Evaluation signing. This license type is available for tuning the device, and the files have

chunks.title: File creation
chunks.text: Signing. The Signing (13) of the files is preset to Evaluation signing. This license type is available for tuning the device, and the files have an evaluation noise. For production/implementation files that do not have an evaluation noise, speak to Dirac.

chunks.title: Resulting files
chunks.text: The Resulting files (14) area shows the files that are generated during the export. An export generates a .DAR file and a .json file, and the .DAR file value shows the calculated file size of the exported file. If the checkbox Create separate resource for each configuration (9) is checked, the Resulting files area shows a .DAR file and a .json file for each configuration. The configuration(s) are exported as .DAR file(s) that contains meta information about the configuration and the interface parameter(s). Additionally, the setup and interface parameters are exported as .json file(s). The export file .DAR and .json pairs must be kept together, as both files are required

chunks.title: Resulting files
chunks.text: setup and interface parameters are exported as .json file(s). The export file .DAR and .json pairs must be kept together, as both files are required for successfully running the files on the device. NOTE: If you have already exported the files before to the same folder, the system sets a warning icon in front of the names of the resulting files. The files that have the the warning icon are overwritten by the new export.

chunks.title: Export recipes
chunks.text: When you have made all the specific the settings you want for an export, you can save the settings as an Export recipe (1). Click on the + icon to save the current setting as an export recipe. You can edit the name of the export recipe to give it a specific name. The export recipes are saved in your workspace and can be used when required.

chunks.title: Export
chunks.text: If you want to close the Export DSP Resources window after the export is done, check the checkbox Close window after export. To export the files to the selected folder, press the Export (15) button. If you want to close the Export DSP Resources window without exporting, press the Close button.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: In Audio Settings, you do the required settings to map the input and output channels for the device when you process audio on your computer or stream audio from the Flow Media player.

chunks.title: Application settings panel
chunks.text: In the Application settings panel (1), set Active application (2) if required. The panel also has the Settings (3) cogwheel to select Theme (dark/light), Save settings as, and Load settings. If you have saved audio settings available, you can load the settings into Audio Settings. Press the Settings (3) cogwheel and select Load settings. Choose the correct settings .json file and press Open. If you want to save your settings, press the Settings (3) cogwheel and select Save settings as. Choose a name for the settings file, select a location, and press Save.

chunks.title: Setup panel
chunks.text: In the Setup panel (4), you can on the input side set the Input type. If applicable, press the Refresh button to update the list of input devices of the selected input type. If the input type and device have any of these settings, you can also set: Input device, Sample rate, Buffer size. On the output side set the Output type. If applicable, press the Refresh button to update the list of output devices of the selected output type. If the output type and device have any of these settings, you can also set: Output device, and if applicable: Sample rate, Buffer size. When you are streaming an output,

chunks.title: Setup panel
chunks.text: device have any of these settings, you can also set: Output device, and if applicable: Sample rate, Buffer size. When you are streaming an output, you must set Host, Port, and press Connect to set up a streaming connection.

chunks.title: Test signal panel
chunks.text: On the Test signal panel (5), you can set the Signal type (Sweep/Pink noise) for the test signal, and increase or decrease Cutoff and Gain.

chunks.title: Channel mapping panel
chunks.text: On the Channel mapping panel (6), the input channels are mapped to the input channels in Flow, and the output channels in Flow are mapped to the device output channels. The Input channels area shows the different configurations from Flow as tabs, and the configuration that is selected in Flow has a microphone icon on the tab. Map each Flow input channel to an input channel from the input device. You can also set the first one and then press the Automatic channel mapping (7) icon to let the application map the other input channels. Each input channel can only be mapped once per configuration. If you want to make

chunks.title: Channel mapping panel
chunks.text: icon to let the application map the other input channels. Each input channel can only be mapped once per configuration. If you want to make different input channel settings for each configuration, check the checkbox Specific settings per configuration. The Output channels area shows the different configurations from Flow as tabs, and the configuration that is selected in Flow has a speaker icon on the tab. Map each Flow output channel to each of the device output channels. You can also press the Automatic channel mapping (8) icon on the Output side to let the application map the channels. Each output channel can only be mapped once. If you want

chunks.title: Channel mapping panel
chunks.text: mapping (8) icon on the Output side to let the application map the channels. Each output channel can only be mapped once. If you want to make different output channel settings for each configuration, check the checkbox Specific settings per configuration.

chunks.title: Processing panel
chunks.text: The Processing panel (9) shows the RT Core version, the connection status, and the selected configuration that is processed. It also makes it possible to adjust the Bypass gain and Overall gain. Check the checkbox Processing enabled to show the processing in the panel. If you uncheck the checkbox, the processing stops. If you click on the profile icon you can sign out of the processing part of Audio Settings.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The utility modules described below are modules that help you inspect, map, view, edit, and play audio.

chunks.title: Volume
chunks.text: Volume is where gain can be applied to a signal or the signal chain. The Ramp control area has settings for the ramp up and ramp down: Link up and down lets you set the same ramp control values for both up and down in one place. Shape sets if the shape is Linear or Logarithmic. Mode sets if the values are shown as Fixed Rate (g/s), Fixed time (ms) or One block. Dynamics shows the value and lets you to edit if the mode is Fixed rate or Fixed time.

chunks.title: Delay
chunks.text: The Delay module lets you set the delay, and you can choose between two different units: Samples or Milliseconds. Press the dot in front of the unit to select the unit for the settings and the view. Delay display in Samples Delay display in Milliseconds

chunks.title: Channel Mapper
chunks.text: Channel mapper lets you map the input channels to the output channels. Click on an element to enable (blue) or disable (grey) it. The module has a Compact and a Full view mode. In Full view mode, the channel names are shown. In Compact view mode, only the channel index is shown. The module also lets you create a diagonal matrix. This clears any previous selection. When you set two or more filter cells for an output channel, the gain automatically merges the filter cell values for the output channel to prevent clipping. It follows the same equation as the 1/N in the Matrix mixer. Refer to the Matrix mixer

chunks.title: Channel Mapper
chunks.text: values for the output channel to prevent clipping. It follows the same equation as the 1/N in the Matrix mixer. Refer to the Matrix mixer page for more information.

chunks.title: Clipper
chunks.text: The output of the Clipper module is clipped at the threshold value. Below this value, audio will go through unaffected. When the Clipping dot is red, it shows that the threshold has been breached and clipping occurs. When the audio is within a range that does not cause clipping, the Clipping dot is green. To prevent clipping, adjust the relevant values until there is no more clipping.

chunks.title: Delay compensation
chunks.text: The Delay compensation module is for inspection of the delay values for defined processors. The delay applied is the sum of the values in the “Compensate for” column minus the sum of the values in the “Already delayed” column. The delay information can be inspected in two different units. Press the dot in front of the unit to select the unit for the view. Inspection display in Samples. Inspection display in Milliseconds

chunks.title: Custom Panel
chunks.text: It is possible to have a customised panel in Flow that has a display for specified levels or parameters. This panel is set up by Dirac on request.

chunks.title: A/B Comparison
chunks.text: If you want to switch between two configurations quickly with one click, you can use A/B-comparison. 1. Select the first configuration you want to include in the comparison in upper left corner of the workspace panel. 2. Go to the A/B-comparison area in the middle of the workspace panel and select from the drop-down list the second configuration you want to include in the comparison. 3. To switch between the two selected configurations, press the A/B button to jump from one to the other. You can also press Shift+F12 to toggle between the two configurations. The configuration that is active is shown as blue.

chunks.title: Media Player
chunks.text: The media player is located on the Media Player tab in the Settings panel. If you use Audio Settings for audio processing, set the input type to Streaming to enable playback of an audio file in Media Player.

chunks.title: To open a media file
chunks.text: Press the Open audio file (1) button to select a file from your computer to upload as a track. The accepted file formats are .wav / .mp3 / .flac / .ogg.

chunks.title: Playback
chunks.text: If you want to adjust the compression of the track for playback, select the compression level in the drop-down list of the Compression (2) field. Press Play (7) to start the playback of the track with the settings you made. If you have checked the checkbox Loop (4), the playback will play within the loop selection (11). Press Back to start (6) to go to the beginning of the track.

chunks.title: Loop
chunks.text: If you want to loop a specific section of the track, use the two dark grey Loop markers (10) to define the loop selection (11). The grey area is the selection that is played in a loop. Check the checkbox Loop (4). Press Play (7) to start the playback. The track now loops infinitely in the defined selection.

chunks.title: Playback position marker
chunks.text: The blue Playback position marker (8) displays the playback position on the track plot. To zoom in on a part of the track, hover over the track plot with the mouse pointer and use the mouse scroll wheel to zoom in. If you want to follow the playback when the plot area is zoomed in, check the checkbox Follow marker (3) to show the position of the Playback position marker (8) when it moves through the track.

chunks.title: Cue position markers
chunks.text: You can set 3 Cue position markers (9) on the track. Drag a cue position with your mouse pointer to the position you want to have it in. When you have set each of the cue position markers, press the Cue position (5) number button to jump to the selected cue position. Media Player

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The compare workspaces feature is a fast way to analyse the differences between two workspaces. All parameters and their values in the two workspaces are exported to a Diff tool, a difference comparison application, where the differences between the files are highlighted.

chunks.title: Diff tool
chunks.text: To be able to use the comparison feature in Flow, you must have a diff tool installed locally on your computer. The application must be able to compare .json files. To set up the diff tool in Flow: 1. Go to the top menu Tools / Options. 2. In the General area, press the dots (2) next to the Diff tool field (1). 3. In the window that opens, open the diff tool program folder. 4. Select the diff tool .exe file on your computer and press Open. The name of the .exe file is now shown in the Diff tool field (1). 5. Set the Argument (3) field value.

chunks.title: Diff tool
chunks.text: and press Open. The name of the .exe file is now shown in the Diff tool field (1). 5. Set the Argument (3) field value. The value can vary between diff tools, for example: %1 %2 or diff %1 %2 6. Press Apply (4).

chunks.title: To compare two workspaces
chunks.text: To start a comparison of two workspaces, go to the top menu Workspace, and select one of the alternatives below to get the diff tool (11) to show the differences.

chunks.title: Compare with saved file
chunks.text: Select Workspace/Compare with saved file to make a comparison of the saved version and the unsaved version of the current workspace.

chunks.title: Compare with other workspace
chunks.text: Select Workspace/Compare with other workspace to make a comparison of the current workspace and another, separate workspace file. In the window that opens, go to the workspace file you want to compare with, select it and press Open.

chunks.title: Advanced compare with other workspace
chunks.text: Select Workspace/Advanced compare with other workspace to make a comparison of the current workspace and another workspace file where the setup and configurations can be selected for the comparison. Press Browse (5) to select the other workspace file you want to compare with. Check the checkboxs (6) to specify what you like to include in the comparison. The checkbox Include all configurations (7) is checked by default, but you can uncheck it to select specific configurations (8) to include in the comparison for each of the workspaces. The Close dialog after diff (9) is checked by default, and it closes the window after the comparison is uploaded into the diff

chunks.title: Advanced compare with other workspace
chunks.text: the workspaces. The Close dialog after diff (9) is checked by default, and it closes the window after the comparison is uploaded into the diff tool. Uncheck the checkbox if you want to keep the window open. Press Diff (10) to upload the comparison into the Diff tool.

chunks.title: To compare two configurations
chunks.text: To start a comparison of two configurations in the same workspace, go to the top menu Workspace/ Compare configurations in this workspace. This opens a specialised version of the Advanced compare dialog, where you can select what to include in the comparison and which configurations to compare. Press Diff (10) to send the comparison to the Diff tool.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Symmetrical submixer processor is a type of Matrix mixer, but without delays. Each input channel can be mapped to an output channel and adjusted for gain. The output channels can be paired and set as a symmetric pair. This is also where you can mix Dimensions.

chunks.title: To create new/import a filter
chunks.text: Press the Create submix (10) button. You can choose to: A. Import filter. This option imports a filter for inspection and editing. You can import multiple filters into the view to inspect them one at a time. B. Create new. Create a blank, editable filter and add filter cells, values and symmetrical pairs as described below. Press the file name to show the filter data in the processor panel (1-8) and properties panel (14- 15). The filter that is shown in the panels has a blue border. To send a specific filter to the device, press the dot (12) before the filter file name. The dot becomes blue for the

chunks.title: To create new/import a filter
chunks.text: blue border. To send a specific filter to the device, press the dot (12) before the filter file name. The dot becomes blue for the filter that is sent to the device.

chunks.title: Spatial settings
chunks.text: Dimensions sets the spatial settings of the symmetrical submixer. A spatial setting must be selected in the Spatial settings (9) field. If you have more than one spatial settings, you can select from the drop-down list a specific setting for the symmetrical submixer.

chunks.title: To edit a filter
chunks.text: You can add and remove filter cells, adjust the values for them, and pair the output so that the two paired output channels become symmetric.

chunks.title: Mute/Solo
chunks.text: Press M (3) on the input/output channel(s) you want to mute. You can mute multiple channels. Press S (3) on the input/output channel(s) you want to listen to on their own. This mutes all other channels. You can select multiple channels as Solo channels.

chunks.title: 1/N
chunks.text: If there are two or more filter cells for an output, you can check the checkbox 1/N (4) to merge the filter cell values for the output channel to prevent clipping.

chunks.title: Filter cell
chunks.text: Click on an unselected, dark grey filter cell (5) in the processor panel to select it. A selected filter cell has a blue border. The cell value is editable both when the cell is selected or unselected. To move a filter cell, drag it to an unused filter cell and drop it in the cell. To add a new filter cell, right-click on an unused, light grey filter cell and select Add element. To copy an existing filter cell, right-click it and select Copy, then right-click an unused filter cell and select Paste. You can also press CTRL, click the filter cell you want to copy, and drag it to

chunks.title: Filter cell
chunks.text: right-click an unused filter cell and select Paste. You can also press CTRL, click the filter cell you want to copy, and drag it to an unused filter cell.

chunks.title: Add symmetric pair
chunks.text: Press the Add symmetric pair (8) button to add a row for pairing. You can pair 2 output channels per row. An output channel can be paired only once. In the pairing row, hover over the pairing cell with the mouse pointer. If the pairing cell becomes dark grey, it can be paired. Click on the first pairing cell for the output channel you want to pair. The cell now has the blue pairing icon (6). Hover over the second output channel pairing cell to make sure it can be paired. If it becomes dark grey, click on it to pair the second output channel. Both channels now have the

chunks.title: Add symmetric pair
chunks.text: make sure it can be paired. If it becomes dark grey, click on it to pair the second output channel. Both channels now have the pairing icon (6) in the same pairing row. If you want to remove the pairing, click on the pairing icon to remove the pairing from an output channel. You can now add the pairing to another output channel in the same row. When two output channels are paired, Flow automatically makes a symmetric setup of filter cells. For each paired output channel, there is a symmetrical setup of filter cells in the channels. Any changes that are made to one of the paired output channel

chunks.title: Add symmetric pair
chunks.text: output channel, there is a symmetrical setup of filter cells in the channels. Any changes that are made to one of the paired output channel filter cells are automatically adjusted in the corresponding output channel filter cell in the paired output channel. Example: When output channel 1 and output channel 2 are paired: If you add filter cells to the input channels Left 2 and Center for output channel 1, Flow automatically adds filter cells to input channels Right 2 and Center for output channel 2. When the gain of Right 2 is adjusted, the gain of Left 2 is automatically adjusted to the same value. NOTE: If the setup

chunks.title: Add symmetric pair
chunks.text: 2. When the gain of Right 2 is adjusted, the gain of Left 2 is automatically adjusted to the same value. NOTE: If the setup includes uncorrelated Dimensions output channels, these are not included in the pairing for the output and are not part of the automatic symmetrical adjustments.

chunks.title: Show attenuated gain
chunks.text: Check the checkbox Show attenuated gain (8) to display the real gain for all filter cells. In this mode, the values of the filter cells and the pairings are not editable.

chunks.title: Lock for editing
chunks.text: Filters can be locked for editing. When you are satisfied with a filter, right-click it and select Lock for editing to prevent unintentional changes. A locked filter shows a padlock icon (16); an unlocked filter has no icon. To make the filter editable again, right-click it and select Unlock. A filter that is imported from a file is locked by default, but it can be unlocked. A filter that is imported with Dirac IO is always locked and cannot be unlocked, because it is controlled by the client. If you want to edit the filter, duplicate it to create an editable copy.

chunks.title: To duplicate a filter
chunks.text: If you want to make an exact copy of a filter, right-click on the filter name and select Duplicate. The copy of the filter is shown in the parameters panel, with a number after the file name.

chunks.title: To export a filter
chunks.text: Right-click the filter you want to export (11 or 12). Select the applicable file format for this filter, and save it to your chosen location. NOTE: Filter export requires an applicable licence.

chunks.title: To remove a filter
chunks.text: Press the minus symbol (13) on the filter you want to remove from the panels. In the popup window, press Delete if you want to remove it, or press Keep to cancel.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Peak limiter processor limits the input signal by setting a maximum threshold value that prevents clipping.

chunks.title: Setup
chunks.text: Set the Linked gain reduction (1) to On to link all channels. You can use it for corresponding channels. If you want to make sure that the Peak limiter is applied and cannot be bypassed, set Force enable (2) to On. The properties (14) show the estimated memory usage and Lookahead value.

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: The Input gain (3) sets the signal gain level for the audio playback input. The Threshold dB (4) sets the signal level for when the gain reduction starts. A lower value gives a harder reduction. The Slow envelope breakpoint (5) sets the gain level for when the slow envelope process is started. The Slow envelope release (6) sets the time for when the slow envelope is stopped after the gain reduction is below the breakpoint. The Slow envelope smoother (7) sets a time constant for smoothing the envelope. NOTE: The slow envelope parameters sets values for the calculated reduction of the gain. The Attack (8) slider sets the time for

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: smoothing the envelope. NOTE: The slow envelope parameters sets values for the calculated reduction of the gain. The Attack (8) slider sets the time for when the full reduction of the gain should be reached. The attack value must be less than 50% of the Lookahead value for best effect. The Hold (9) slider sets the time for how long the audio should be sustained at the same level before it is released. The Release (10) slider set the time for how long it should take until the gain has returned to 0 dB. NOTE: Overshoots can still occur if the relation between Attack, Hold, and Lookahead times are not

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: take until the gain has returned to 0 dB. NOTE: Overshoots can still occur if the relation between Attack, Hold, and Lookahead times are not balanced. You can adjust Attack and Hold times as needed to prevent overshoots. The Lookahead time is a fixed value that is set for the signal chain.

chunks.title: Level meters
chunks.text: The level meters at the bottom of the processor panel shows: The Input meter (11) shows the input levels from the playback. The Gain meter (12) shows the applied gain levels of the peak limiter processing. The Output meter (13) shows the output levels after processing.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Reverb processor is where the reverb response is calculated according to the Schroeder reverb algorithm.

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: The Pre-delay (1) slider sets the time in milliseconds for the length of the pause before the onset of the reverb signal. The T60 (2) slider sets the time in which the reverb signal should decrease by -60 dB. The Room size (3) value corresponds to an estimated room volume for the calculation of the reverb. Setting a higher the value results in a larger room impression of the reverb. The High frequency damping (4) slider sets the percentage of how much the high frequencies should be dampened. The Dry/Wet (5) slider sets the balance between the reverb signal and a passthrough of the input signal.

chunks.title: Level meters
chunks.text: The level meters at the bottom of the processor panel shows meters for: The Input meter (6) shows the input levels from the playback. The Output meter (7) shows the output levels after processing.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: The properties (8) show the estimated memory usage, latency, the number of comb filters, maximum pre-delay, maximum room size and the usage of half float delay lines.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The AGC (Automatic Gain Control) processor is where the input signal is analysed and calculated against the target level. The AGC applies slow changes that makes the user perceive the audio at the same gain level.

chunks.title: Setup
chunks.text: Set the Channel link (10) to On to link corresponding input channels (for example Left and Right) to apply the same gain to all channels.

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: The Target level (2) slider sets the intended level for the output signal. The Max reduction (3) slider sets maximum permitted gain reduction for the audio. The Max gain boost (4) slider sets the maximum permitted gain increase when there is a weak input signal. The Freeze level (5) slider sets the level for when the AGC processor should stop processing the input signal. Signal levels below the set Freeze level are not processed. The Max change rate (6) slider sets the maximum speed at which changes should be applied for the output. The Attack time (7) controls the attack of the envelope-following of the input signal. The Hold time

chunks.title: Settings
chunks.text: which changes should be applied for the output. The Attack time (7) controls the attack of the envelope-following of the input signal. The Hold time (8) controls the hold of the envelope-following of the input signal. The Release time (9) controls the release of the envelope-following of the input signal.

chunks.title: Level meters
chunks.text: The level meters at the bottom of the processor panel shows meters for: The Input meter (10) shows the input levels. The Gain meter (11) shows the currently applied gain. The Output meter (12) shows the output levels after processing.
